_note: Per-post thematic summaries from TAO analysis. Each entry is a list of theme statements — concise, opinionated one-liners about what the post argues. These also live in each post's frontmatter as 'themes:'.
nora-bateson-how-our-ways-of-knowing-sha: Applying static, context-free data to living systems is dangerous
Warm data contextualises information through relationships, as an alternative to reductionism
Systems thinking as an ethical stance, inherited from Gregory Bateson
is-conversation-still-a-useful-metaphor: Conversation metaphor as increasingly inadequate for GenAI
Anthropomorphism as a structural side effect of conversation design
Alternative interaction metaphors: delegation, thinking, note-taking
Metacognition and inner dialog as possible paradigms for human-AI interaction
why-chatgpt-is-bullshit-and-why-we-shoul: LLMs as structurally indifferent to truth, not accidentally wrong
Grice's cooperative principle as the violated contract
Cognitive laziness as the human vulnerability that makes this dangerous
Design as the response: keeping humans caring about truth
conversational-interfaces-are-not-easy: Conversational interfaces are poorly suited to non-linear tasks like writing
Two new AI user behaviors: accordion editing and apple picking
The articulation barrier as a specific usability threshold
Direct manipulation as the design response
context-engineering-lets-call-it-design: Context engineering is a rebranding of work designers and authors have always done
Semantic information types as the structural logic behind good context windows
Design vocabulary maps directly onto prompt engineering: information architecture, instructional design, technical authoring
Inviting designers and authors to the GenAI table as a practical recommendation
llm-hallucinations-knowledge-as-missing-: LLM hallucinations are structurally unsolvable without changing the underlying mechanism
Confabulation as a more precise term: filling gaps with plausible fabrications, not random errors
The missing fundamental as an analogy: truth can only be approximated in LLMs, never caught
The impossibility of a genuine TRUE/FALSE binary state in probabilistic systems
thinking-in-action-precision-matters: Precise terminology as a prerequisite for clear thinking
Dialectical thinking as the antidote to epistemic bias
The distinction between opinion, conviction, argument, and rhetoric
LLMs reinforce rather than correct our tendency to avoid dialectical challenge
a-digital-garden-as-central-space: The early web enabled a kind of personal expression that the algorithm era has taken away
Non-linear thinking needs a non-linear writing environment — not a blog, not a social feed
A digital garden is the right infrastructure for how my mind actually works
Serendipity is an organising principle, not a side effect
Writing as craft requires a space that doesn't talk back and doesn't distract
AI has a legitimate role in the garden, but only as assistant — never as author
chatgpt-presentation-prep: The value of AI as a feedback loop lies not in the quality of its output but in the quality of articulation it provokes from the user.
Procrastination and presentation anxiety are often articulation problems, not motivation problems — and that reframes what a useful tool looks like.
Voice-mode AI works because it removes the pressure of judgment while preserving the benefit of an audience, a combination humans rarely offer.
Iterative spoken rehearsal with transcription is a legitimate structured methodology, even when the AI's analytical feedback is mediocre.
Fitting a tool to a cognitive style is more powerful than forcing a cognitive style to fit a tool.
7-new-skills-for-conversation-designers-: The content/code boundary is a false constraint: conversation designers who learn NLU and Python become fundamentally more capable, not just more versatile.
Entities, not intents, are the underexploited building block of robust conversational systems — a systematic entity model is the conversation designer's equivalent of an information architecture.
Knowledge graphs represent the logical ceiling of entity thinking: they transform a conversational interface from a command-and-response tool into a navigable semantic universe.
Conversational AI sits uncomfortably between IT and content, and that organisational ambiguity is itself a design problem that practitioners must learn to solve.
Skill expansion for conversation designers in 2022 is not about chasing trends but about closing the gap between what language professionals know and what the technology now demands.
instagram: Claude Code's plugin ecosystem frames AI capabilities as professional team roles
Plugins as delegation: assigning developer responsibilities to specialized agentic tools
air-canadas-bot-mishap-pre-dates-chatgpt: The Air Canada chatbot story is routinely misread as an LLM failure, when it was actually a mundane content governance failure that predates generative AI entirely.
Content siloes are the real enemy of reliable conversational AI — not model capability or hallucination.
Single sourcing — write once, configure for many — is the structural solution to cross-channel content inconsistency, whether your bot is NLU-based or LLM-based.
Content should be treated as structured, granular, metadated data rather than freeform prose, to enable omnichannel consistency.
The tooling problem in conversational AI is not just about the model; it's about dashboards that expose content component relationships, channel dependencies, and release provenance.
